newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-British yachtsman's aunt waits for reunion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-British yachtsman's aunt waits for reunion.

text.p: The 81-year old aunt of rescued British yachtsman Tony Bullimore despaired of ever seeing her nephew again, and not just because his yacht capsized in icy waters near the Antartica.
Every time Dinah Twomey, who has lived in Perth for over 20 years, returned to Britain to see her family Bullimore was away sailing.
"I haven't seen Tony for over 20 years because every time we went back he was off sailing or doing other things so we wondered if we'd see him again," Twomey told Reuters from her home near Perth.
Bullimore survived for four days inside an air pocket in the hull of his upturned yacht before being rescued earlier on Wednesday by the crew of an Australian frigate.
He is now expected to arrive back in Perth on Monday and his immediate family and his Aunt are hoping to greet him as the frigate docks at the Perth port of Fremantle.
"It's not the best way to get a family reunion, but we'll take it. I'm just so relieved he's alright," Twomey said.
"Underneath we always thought he'd make it through. He's very strong and very resourceful," she said.
Officials said Bullimore, 56, managed to climb free from his upturned yacht after rescuers from the HMAS Adelaide knocked on its hull to see if he was still alive.

Bullimore's rescue capped a day of drama in the southern Indian Ocean. Hours earlier, fellow solo yachtsman Frenchman Thierry Dubois was winched to safety by a helicopter from the same frigate after four days drifting in a life raft in heavy seas.
Both men, who were competing in the Vendee Globe round-the-world yacht race, were reported to be in surprisingly good shape despite their ordeal.
Twomey however joined in criticising race organisers for allowing competitors to go so far south to speed their passages.
"I don't think they should go that far south, with those seas and winds they have down there. It's just too dangerous," she said.
